objective.statement: Add a second torus widget to HomeView.tsx; the second torus must be red.

complexity.rationale: TorusWidget hard-codes green with no props, so a red instance needs a small, backwards-compatible colour prop on the component as well as a second mount in HomeView, and one existing HomeView test asserts a single widget. Still two presentational files, no state, API or dependency change.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: HomeView renders two torus widgets: the existing green one and a second one whose torus is red (data-color "red"; fill and gradient stops use red hex values, no green).
TorusWidget rendered without props is unchanged: still green with the same geometry (150px outer diameter, 6px ring), size (no bigger than 200px by 200px) and label.
The red torus has the same geometry, gradient shape, widget size and label as the green one; only the colour differs.

in.statement: HomeView.tsx (mount a second TorusWidget after the first), TorusWidget.tsx (optional colour prop, default green, adding a red palette), and the matching component tests for both.

out.statement: Torus geometry, widget size, label text, other HomeView widgets and layout, theme tokens, dependencies, and historical workflow records.

observations.statement: TorusWidget.tsx takes no props and hard-codes TORUS_GREEN #16a34a, TORUS_GREEN_LIGHT #4ade80, TORUS_GREEN_DARK #14532d and data-color="green". HomeView mounts it once, as the last child of the section.
The card names no exact red. Assumed the same Tailwind family as the green: base #dc2626, light #f87171, dark #7f1d1d, keeping the gradient shape.

Colour is chosen by a new optional prop on TorusWidget (color: "green" | "red", default "green") rather than a copied component, so the default render and existing tests are unchanged. No new dependency or contract for other consumers: the prop is optional.
The second widget is placed directly after the first, at the end of HomeView. The card gives no position; the end of the section is the smallest layout change.

Both widgets keep the label "Torus Widget" and aria-label "Torus Widget", and the same data-id test ids. The card does not ask for a different label; changing it would be a user-visible decision. Consequence: HomeView test 'should render the torus widget' uses getByTestId and would throw on two matches, so it is intentionally changed to assert two widgets. The torus-level test is scoped by colour rather than by id.

Two sections share the accessible name "Torus Widget". The torus svg is aria-hidden, so the label text is the only cue; screen-reader users cannot tell the two apart. Accepted for now per ob-5; the owner may ask for distinct labels.

capabilityOwners.owner: none (stateless presentational component; colour comes from a prop)
capabilityOwners.rationale: No UI state; the colour is a render-time prop.

component.rationale: The rendered colour of the torus and the number of widgets on HomeView are the behaviours under change.

integration.rationale: HomeView composition is covered by its component test; no routing, store or API interaction.

e2e.rationale: Static visual addition with no user flow.

increments.behavior: TorusWidget accepts an optional colour and renders a red torus when asked, staying green by default.
increments.doneWhen: The red-torus component test passes and every existing TorusWidget test still passes unchanged.

increments.behavior: HomeView renders two torus widgets, the second red.
increments.doneWhen: The HomeView two-widgets test passes and the other HomeView tests still pass.

tests.description: TorusWidget rendered with color="red" has data-color "red", fill and every gradient stop a red hex (#dc2626, #f87171, #7f1d1d) and none of the green values.

HomeView renders exactly two torus widgets, one with a green torus and one with a red torus. Replaces the single-widget assertion in 'should render the torus widget', which cannot hold with two widgets (ob-5).

expectedRedEvidence.expectedFailure: Expected data-color "red" but received "green" (the prop is ignored or does not exist yet).
Expected two torus widgets but found one; no red torus on HomeView.

verification.requirement: npm run test:component passes; npm run lint and npm run build are clean
